topic: How long do the effects of a massage last?

slides.headline: How long does that looser feeling last?
slides.sub: The honest answer about massage, and how to make it go further.

slides.title: Usually hours to a few days
slides.body: Most people feel looser and more relaxed for somewhere between a few hours and a few days. It varies with your body, stress, sleep and what you do afterwards.

slides.title: Why the effect fades
slides.body: Massage mainly changes how muscles and nerves feel, rather than changing tissue for good. If the habits that built the tightness come back, the tightness often does too.

slides.title: Move while it feels easier
slides.body: The window after a massage is a great time to move. A walk, some gentle mobility or your home exercises that evening can help you hold onto that easier feeling.

slides.title: Change the daily load
slides.body: If your shoulders tighten after every long desk day, small changes like regular breaks and a strength routine often do more to extend the effect than booking more often.

slides.title: Find a rhythm that suits you
slides.body: Some people book every few weeks in busy seasons and less often otherwise. Your remedial massage therapist can help you work out what's realistic for your goals and budget.

slides.headline: Want your massage to go further?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists pair hands-on work with simple things you can do between sessions. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Walked out of your massage feeling brand new, then two days later the tight shoulders were back?

That's pretty normal. For most people, the looser, calmer feeling lasts somewhere between a few hours and a few days. Massage changes how your muscles and nerves feel, and if the same habits keep loading you up, the tightness tends to return.

The good news: you can stretch that window. Move while things feel easier, keep up any home exercises, and look at the daily load, like long unbroken desk stretches, that keeps winding you up.
